title: Prepositions of Place & Movement
subtitle: Say exactly where something is, and how it moves.
objectives: Use prepositions of place (in, on, at, under, behind, next to, between, among) to say where things are
Use prepositions of movement (into, onto, out of, through, over, along, towards, across) to say how something moves

content.intro: At A1 you learned basic in/on/at. Now let's expand your toolkit for describing exact position and movement.

rules.heading: a) Place — where something is (no movement)
rules.body: under, behind, next to, between (two things), among (three or more things), in front of, near

rules.heading: b) Movement — how something moves
rules.body: into (entering), onto (getting on top of), out of (leaving), through (from one side to the other, inside something), over (above, crossing), along (following a line, like a road or river), towards (in the direction of), across (from one side to the other, on a surface)

examples: The cat is under the table.
He walks through the park to go to school.
She sits between her two best friends.
The keys are in my bag.
The dog jumps into the pool.

commonMistakes.wrong: She sits between her three friends.
commonMistakes.right: She sits among her three friends.
commonMistakes.why: "Between" is for two things/people; "among" is for three or more.

commonMistakes.wrong: The dog jumps in the pool. (describing the action of jumping in)
commonMistakes.right: The dog jumps into the pool.
commonMistakes.why: "Into" describes movement from outside to inside; "in" only describes position, not movement.

commonMistakes.wrong: He walks across the park. (through the middle, not on a flat surface like a road)
commonMistakes.why: "Through" fits movement inside/across an area like a park; "across" is more natural for a flat, open surface like a road or field.

exercises.title: Fill in the Blanks
exercises.instructions: Complete each sentence with the correct preposition.

items.prompt: She sits ___ her best friend at the concert.
items.explanation: "Next to" for being right beside one person.
"Along" for following the line of the river.
Crossing from one side to the other — "across."

items.prompt: She stands ___ the two trees. (two things)
He walks ___ the crowd. (a large group, more than two)
items.explanation: "Among" for three or more, like a crowd.

items.incorrect: She sits between her three friends.
answer: She sits among her three friends.
items.explanation: Three or more people needs "among," not "between."

items.incorrect: The children run in the playground. (arriving, entering)
answer: The children run into the playground.
items.explanation: Movement into a place needs "into," not just "in."

summary: Place (no movement): under, behind, next to, between (2), among (3+).
Movement: into/onto (entering) vs. out of (leaving); through/across/along/towards describe how something moves.
Between is only for two things; among is for three or more.
